title: Local Galactic Structures, Clusters & Deep Sky

structures.name: Hyades Cluster
structures.description: The nearest open star cluster to the Solar System, sharing a common trajectory through space.

structures.name: Coma Star Cluster
structures.description: A loose, prominent open cluster located high above the galactic plane in Coma Berenices.

structures.name: Ursa Major Moving Group
structures.description: A co-moving stellar kinematic group containing the core stars of the Big Dipper.

structures.name: Pleiades (Seven Sisters)
structures.description: Luminous young open cluster just beyond the 100-pc boundary, prominent in night-sky lore.

structures.name: Praesepe (Beehive Cluster)
structures.description: One of the nearest open clusters, sharing similar age and proper motion to the Hyades.

structures.name: IC 2602 (Southern Pleiades)
structures.description: Bright young open cluster surrounding Theta Carinae in the southern sky.

structures.name: IC 2391 (Omicron Velorum Cluster)
structures.description: Compact open cluster in Vela visible to the naked eye.

structures.name: Alpha Persei Cluster
structures.description: Young OB stellar association surrounding Mirfak in Perseus.

structures.name: Messier 4 (M4)
structures.description: The closest globular cluster to the Solar System, situated in Scorpius near Antares.

structures.name: NGC 6397
structures.description: One of the oldest known globular clusters in the Milky Way with a core-collapsed structure.

structures.name: Omega Centauri
structures.description: The largest and most massive globular cluster in the Milky Way; remnant nucleus of a dwarf galaxy.

structures.name: Messier 13 (Great Hercules Cluster)
structures.description: The premier northern sky globular cluster in the constellation Hercules.

structures.name: Vela Supernova Remnant
structures.description: A massive expanding filamentary remnant of a stellar explosion occurring ~11,000 years ago.

structures.name: Cygnus Loop (Veil Nebula)
structures.description: Spectacular optical emission nebula marking a core-collapse supernova remnant in Cygnus.

structures.name: Crab Nebula (M1)
structures.description: Pulsar wind plerion remnant created by the historical supernova of 1054 recorded by Chinese astronomers.

structures.name: Helix Nebula
structures.description: The closest planetary nebula to Earth, showing a dying low-mass star shedding its outer gas shell.

structures.name: Dumbbell Nebula
structures.description: The first planetary nebula discovered in history, notable for its bright hourglass morphology in Vulpecula.

structures.name: Local Interstellar Cloud (LIC)
structures.description: Warm diffuse gas cloud through which Sol is currently passing within the low-density Local Bubble.

structures.name: Geminga
structures.description: Radio-quiet gamma-ray pulsar and neutron star created by an ancient local supernova.

structures.name: PSR J0108-1431
structures.description: One of the oldest and closest known isolated radio pulsars to Earth.

structures.name: Vela Pulsar
structures.description: Rapidly rotating neutron star (period: 89 ms) powering the central filaments of the Vela SNR.
